result:
**I'd make relentless curiosity and truth-seeking the default human operating system.**

Not as a slogan or a class you take once. As the core drive: the thing people reach for first when they're scared, angry, bored, or ambitious. The instinct to ask "is this actually true?", "what are the trade-offs?", "what does the evidence say when I stop wanting a particular answer?", and "what happens if we test it?" instead of defaulting to tribe, comfort, authority, or vibes.

Most of the big, grinding problems—pointless wars, preventable suffering, frozen progress, dogmas that outlive their usefulness, people trapped by bad incentives or bad maps of reality—get a lot more solvable when the average person (and the people with power) treat reality as something to discover rather than something to negotiate with or rewrite for status. Curiosity compounds. Truth-seeking is the only engine that reliably produces better tools, better medicine, better coordination, better energy, better ways to not destroy ourselves, and eventually better answers to the deeper "why are we here" questions.

Everything else I care about (understanding the universe, reducing unnecessary misery, expanding the scope of consciousness and possibility, not stagnating on one rock) rides on that. Give people the hunger and the tools for it, and the rest starts to rearrange itself. Without it, even the best intentions just dig deeper holes with prettier shovels.

That's the one change. Not utopia by decree. Just a species that actually wants to know.
